//InsectPlague: The insect plague's timer: a self-timed effect stat (Documentation/Research/HarshWilds/events_stats.md sections 1c skeleton (c) and 4c, its insect plague DECISION), the shape of hw_stat_drought. Written ONLY by the Insect Plague collection of SelfTriggeredAction/Tgr_HW_InsectPlague.json (+HW_PLAGUE_TICKS = 288, its max, 3 days), then counts itself down at BaseRatePerTick -1 and rests at 0. While it reads 1 to HW_PLAGUE_TICKS its one status is active: it raises a Moderate alert when the plague starts (NotifyPlayer 2 NotifyWhenGoingUp, AlertLevel 2 Moderate) and shows the vanilla sprite Bugs in the status strip (Visibility 0 VisibleWithStatus and StatusesHaveNoBar true, the drought's shape; Visibility 2 would be NeverVisible and hide the alert). The status ANNOUNCES ONLY and has no EffectsOnStats on purpose: a status effect is a GlobalModifier on the whole run, and an insect plague must bite outdoors only. The bite is delivered by SelfTriggeredAction/Tgr_HW_PlagueSwarm.json, which reads this timer as a gate and refreshes the hidden hw_stat_bugswarm on every tick the player is outdoors while this timer runs; hw_stat_bugswarm's status raises the vanilla BugPopulation. The plague ENDS when this stat reaches 0: the swarm is no longer refreshed and is gone two ticks later. HW_PLAGUE_TICKS = 288 (MinMaxValue.y, the status's ValueRange.y and the arm in Tgr_HW_InsectPlague) is a TUNABLE PLACEHOLDER, session-inferred and unmeasured against play; the status text says 'about three days', so retune it together with the text. Vanilla InsectProtection is NOT a counter for this plague (it only lowers Mosquitoes, MEASURED in events_stats.md section 0) and no player text says it is.

Description.DefaultText: A summer insect plague. Biting insects swarm outdoors until it passes.

Swarms of biting insects have come, for about three days. Outdoors you will be bitten far more than usual, and the bites add up. Rain, a fire at your camp (campfire, fire pit, fireplace or hearth), snakegrass fed to a hearth, and staying indoors all thin them out.
